card.name: Kintauri
card.era: Urban dance of old Tiflis (19th c.)
card.tagline: Cheeky street dance of old Tbilisi's merchants
card.profile: Kintauri, also Kintouri, portrays the city life of old Tbilisi and is named after the 'kintos' - small, cunning street merchants who wore black outfits with baggy trousers and carried goods on their heads (Wikipedia). When a customer chose produce, a kinto would weigh it in a silk shawl drawn from his silver belt. The light-natured dance captures the kinto's swift, informal, sly character. It is closely associated with the related Shalakho and is part of the urban Tbilisi repertoire alongside Karachokheli and Davluri (Georgia About).
card.insight: Kintauri preserves the social memory of multi-ethnic 19th-century Tiflis street commerce, dramatizing the figure of the kinto as a comic, streetwise urban type rather than the warriors or aristocrats of other Georgian dances.
card.image_significance: The cheeky street-merchant dance of Tbilisi. A representative image shows upright carriage, sweeping arm lines and embroidered dress — old Tbilisi, Georgia.
